stories.title: Pakistan’s new UN envoy presents credentials to secretary general in New York
summary: UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan’s newly appointed Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, presented his credentials to UN Secretary General António Guterres at UN Headquarters in New York on Tuesday.
A senior career diplomat, Ambassador Shah had served as Pakistan’s ambassador to the Netherlands since March 2025, and was posted in Nepal from 2020 to 2022.

Prior to that, from 2002 to 2006, he was posted at Pakistan’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York, where he covered the General Assembly’s Sixth Committee and participated in negotiations on UN Security Council (UNSC) and General Assembly resolutions.

stories.title: Imran's nephew denied jail meeting this time; PTI open to possible alliance with JUI-F
summary: ISLAMABAD: PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was again denied a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday – a prescribed day by the Islamabad High Court for meetings at the Adiala jail.

Chaudhry, whose name was also included in the list, said that lawyers, including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, also reached the prison, but were not allowed to meet the ex-premier.

Gohar refutes rumour that Imran ‘happy’ about KP governor’s rule Separately, the PTI chairman dismissed the notion that Imran himself wanted his party’s government in KP to be sacked and was happy with the imposition of governor’s rule. “It is not correct,” Barrister Gohar said.

stories.title: Americans vote in midterm election seen as a referendum on Trump presidency
summary: Americans voted on Tuesday in a midterm election seen as a nationwide referendum on US President Donald Trump that could wrest control of Congress from his Republican Party and impose major restraints on the remaining two years of his presidency.

Trump, who will watch the midterm results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress, he could simply defy Democrats. “I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

stories.title: Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews, malicious code in $6.3bn heist
summary: Binance released on Tuesday a detailed investigation into the $6.3 billion hack of its cryptocurrency platform, showing how attackers used fake job interviews and malicious code to steal the funds.
Binance says outflows normalised as North Korea rejects US allegation Asset outflows from Binance have normalised and the company was in “very strong financial health”, its co-CEO said.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on the weekend that North Korea was responsible for the theft of more than $6bn in crypto assets, a crime that sent shockwaves through the industry.

stories.title: Govt assures public of meeting gas demand in winter, pledges to ensure supply during mealtimes
summary: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Tuesday assured the public that the government will make utmost efforts to meet the demand for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) during the winter months.
In his press briefing today, Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for LPG.
Malik elaborated that the total demand for LPG was approximately 2.4 million tonnes, amounting to about 6,500 to 7,000 tonnes per day.

stories.title: YouTube viewership in Pakistan records surge
summary: TikTok has around 100 million users in Pakistan, while nearly 150 million videos are watched and uploaded on the platform daily from the country, the National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunications was told on Tuesday.

He told the committee that 96 million Pakistanis currently use YouTube and watch around 560 million videos on the platform every day, making Pakistan the world's leading country in terms of YouTube video viewership.
The government had taken steps to improve telecom services, she added.

stories.title: Committee warns GSP+ access at risk
summary: The standing committee also expressed disappointment over yet another failed trader scheme, as the government announced enforcement action against all traders except the 222 who joined, subject to approval by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Trade scheme fails The standing committee expressed disappointment over the failure of the fixed tax scheme for traders, as only 222 new shopkeepers joined against a hope of one million out of 3.7 million non-filers.
"The government is very much committed to take action and we are preparing an enforcement plan for the approval of the prime minister," Kayani said.

stories.title: Ishrat's reforms yet to be implemented
summary: December 1999, Pakistan had been left with only $300 million in foreign exchange reserves due to crippling economic sanctions and international isolation and at that time military ruler General Pervez Musharraf appointed Dr Ishrat Husain to turn around the central bank.
After leaving the central bank following two maximum stints, Husain did not rest and contributed to improving economic governance and civil service reforms.
Ghana was the first country that embraced the World Bank's structural reforms, and it is today a success story, Husain said.

stories.title: UAE investors invited into eight sectors
summary: LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar put the proposals to Salem Mohammed Al Zaabi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Pakistan, at a meeting on bilateral commercial relations, according to a statement issued on Tuesday.
He said closer engagement could open new avenues for trade and investment.

stories.title: ECC asks about placement of trained agri-experts
summary: The Ministry of Education briefed the ECC that the prime minister during his visit to China in June 2024 had said that 1,000 Pakistani agricultural professionals be trained in China to benefit from its expertise in agricultural technology, innovation and research.

The Ministry of Education recalled that the ECC, in its meeting held on November 28, 2024, had approved a technical supplementary grant of Rs3,072 million for implementation of the programme in batches.
The Ministry of Federal Education apprised the ECC that during FY2025-26 HEC placed a further 593 trainees in two batches, bringing the total number of trained agricultural professionals to 885.

stories.title: Kazakhstan sets five-year trade roadmap with Pakistan
summary: Kazakhstan's deputy prime minister expressed his desire for Pakistan's prime minister to visit Kazakhstan and reaffirmed his country's commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.
The deputy prime minister also highlighted the need for direct air connectivity between Pakistan and Kazakhstan to facilitate business, trade and people-to-people exchanges.

The statement said the meeting focused on stronger trade, investment and connectivity ties, with both sides exploring ways to increase bilateral trade and new investment opportunities between Pakistan and Kazakhstan.

stories.title: CM Maryam sends Rs 5b legal notices to Salik Hussain, TV channel over corruption remarks
summary: The notices contend that Salik made sweeping allegations about corruption in Punjab without providing any evidence to substantiate them, damaging the reputation of the chief minister and the provincial administration.

It is pertinent to mention that Salik Hussain's brother, Chaudhry Shafay Hussain, is also part of the provincial government and serves directly under Maryam Nawaz as Punjab's minister for industries, commerce and investment.

Responding to Salik’s criticism of the use of official aircraft, Bokhari said Maryam Nawaz was the first Punjab chief minister to personally bear the expenses incurred through the use of the government aircraft.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers stage fourth day of wage protests
summary: Garment workers in Bangladesh staged a fourth day of wage protests on Tuesday, with police firing tear gas to disperse demonstrators as unrest disrupted factory operations and transport links in the country’s vital export sector.

The unrest, which began on Saturday, has intensified despite the government’s move to form a six-member wage board to review pay in Bangladesh’s garment sector, the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China.
They warn that prolonged unrest could disrupt production schedules and jeopardise export orders, while workers continue to press for higher wages and better working conditions.

stories.title: Spanish footballer Jesus De Miguel dies after collision with keeper
summary: Andorra also sent their “most sincere condolences” to De Miguel’s family, team-mates and Tenerife.
Real Madrid held a minute of silence before their training session on Tuesday. “Immense sadness, there are no words,” Madrid’s French forward Kylian Mbappe wrote on Instagram.

Other sports stars, including Rafa Nadal and Lionel Messi also left messages on Instagram. “There are no words… rest in peace,” wrote Inter Miami forward Messi. “What a terrible sadness… I’m with you from the bottom of my heart,” wrote Nadal.

stories.title: CM Maryam incensed at Chaudhry Salik's claims of corruption in Punjab, sends him Rs5bn defamation notice
summary: LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks.
Maryam also took exception to Salik’s comments calling Elahi the “best-ever chief minister” in Punjab. “The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining.

It stated that the chief minister considered the conduct of all three individuals named in the notice “serious and unacceptable”: Salik for his “false statements”, Butt for his editorial conduct and Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegations.

stories.title: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR
summary: According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces conducted the IBOs on Nov 1 on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan”.

During the operation, “terrorists’ attempt to establish [a] road block in the city was thwarted by proactive action of security forces,“ resulting in the killing of 10 terrorists. “Weapons and ammunition were also recovered,” it added.

He also paid tribute to the martyred soldier, saying that the “brave sons of the security forces are a source of pride for the nation”. “The security forces remain committed to the complete eradication of Indian-sponsored terrorists,” he said.

stories.title: Islamabad ATC grants bail to Imaan, Hadi in police altercation case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Tuesday granted bail to lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, in a case registered against them for allegedly blocking a road outside the National Press Club and engaging in an altercation with police.
The police also produced the case record before the court during the proceedings.
Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case.

stories.title: IHC issues notices on plea seeking criminal proceedings in PIMS nursery fire
summary: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal government and others in a petition seeking registration of a case over the deaths of children in the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) tragedy and compensation for the affected families.

Read: 14 newborns killed in fire at PIMS Hospital in Islamabad The court also summoned the complete record, including the inquiry report into the incident, and suspended an order passed by a justice of the peace dismissing an application for registration of an FIR.
The petitioner told the court that 14 children had caught fire simultaneously in the PIMS incident, while another child died later.

stories.title: JI and Dar hold 'candid discussions' on fuel relief, agree to continue talks in coming days
summary: The government and Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) on Tuesday held “candid discussions” on practical measures to provide relief to low-income citizens in petroleum prices.

After a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last week, both sides agreed to form a bipartisan committee to expand the government’s ongoing fuel relief scheme in response to JI’s demands for the abolition of the petroleum levy.

When PM Shehbaz and Rehman finally met about a month later, they agreed to form a joint committee to recommend proposals for expanding the fuel relief scheme and for a phased reduction in the petroleum levy for the next budget.

stories.title: Trump says US is close to making a trade deal with Canada
summary: President Donald Trump said on ​Tuesday the United States was close ‌to making a trade deal with Canada.
Trump and Canadian Prime Minister ​Mark ​Carney said on ⁠Sunday they had spoken about a trade deal, which the ​US president said would be "great ​for ⁠our farmers".

Trump had also emphasised that the arrangement would dismantle Canadian agricultural trade barriers, asserting that "our farmers were paying tremendous tariffs to send things to Canada", reaching up to 400% on dairy items.

stories.title: IHC grants TikToker Anser Mahmood protective bail in wedding stampede case
summary: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Anser Mahmood, alias "Mr Patlu", who was nominated in a case registered over culpable homicide, unlawful assembly, rioting and the death of one person and injuries to several others in a stampede.
A prize draw at a TikToker's wedding celebration on Sunday turned deadly after a stampede at Faraz Ground in Daska left two people dead and 17 others injured.
The petitioner argued that the IHC had the authority to grant protective bail to enable him to approach the relevant court for pre-arrest bail without examining the merits of the case.

stories.title: Entertainer and enigma, Glenn Maxwell bows out as cricket's great what-if
summary: A two-time ODI World Cup winner, Maxwell also hit the winning runs in Australia’s maiden T20 World Cup triumph in 2021 under captain Aaron Finch.

You’ve changed the way the game is played and inspired so many along the way.” T20 royalty Maxwell’s value was always three-dimensional: explosive batting, savvy off-spin, and electric fielding that saved runs and snared jaw-dropping catches.
Maxwell played only seven tests between 2013 and 2017, scoring 339 runs at a modest average of 26.

stories.title: Lahore court grants NCCIA further two-day remand of suspects over US postage stamp fraud
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) a further two-day physical remand of two suspects in a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps.
The Lahore NCCIA announced the prime suspect’s arrest in late October, and he was sent on a five-day physical remand on Oct 21.
According to NCCIA, the initial investigation revealed that the prime suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake US postage stamps over a period of more than three years.

stories.title: Gohar refutes reports of Imran welcoming end of K-P government
summary: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday rejected media reports suggesting that party founder Imran Khan had welcomed the end of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government, saying he had made no such statement during his meeting at Adiala jail with Barrister Salman Safdar.
Any decision about the provincial government or a possible candidate for the chief minister’s office would be taken by the party founder, he added. “Everyone will act according to Imran’s views.
He welcomed Safdar’s meeting with Imran, saying restrictions on access to the PTI founder had fuelled political tensions.

stories.title: European supermarkets rush to patch vulnerabilities after region-wide fridge hack
summary: Stores in ‌eight European countries were forced to throw away vast quantities of food after hackers tampered with their fridges on Monday, in an attack identical to one that swept dozens of supermarkets in France three weeks ago.

Read: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe The seven stores hit by the attack are back up and running, but their refrigeration systems have ​been disconnected from the internet, a spokesperson said.

German supermarket operator ​Edeka, which had fridges hacked at ⁠a store in Reisbach, Germany, told Reuters there are no standardised refrigeration systems across its network of stores run by independent retailers.

stories.title: IHC grants protective bail to TikToker booked following stampede at wedding event
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, after a stampede at his mehndi (henna) event in Sialkot claimed two lives.

On Tuesday, IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar approved the protective — also known as transitory — bail for the TikToker until Nov 10, allowing him to avoid arrest while he approaches the relevant court to seek legal remedy.
Jatt had filed a petition, seeking the court’s intervention to prevent his arrest before he could reach the court of competent jurisdiction.

stories.title: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer
summary: France has opened a judicial investigation into a war crimes complaint over an Israeli strike on a residential building in Lebanon, a lawyer told AFP on Tuesday.
Several investigations underway While the judicial investigation marks a first over alleged war crimes by Israeli forces in Lebanon, other cases are pending.

The PNAT also asked a Paris judge to open a war crimes investigation into the deaths of two French children in an Israeli bombing in Gaza in October 2023, while ruling out charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, according to sources close to the case.

stories.title: Nine things on US voters' minds ahead of midterm elections: poll
summary: The cost of living Some 48% of registered voters in the poll say the cost of living is the top issue for deciding how they will vote, compared with 26% who say democratic norms and 13% who point to ​immigration.

The Reuters/Ipsos poll showed ⁠that 48% of people who planned to vote — or already had done so — said they thought of their ballots as a vote against Trump, ​compared to 25% who said they were voting for him.
Some 43% of registered voters in the poll said Democrats ​had at least some good ideas, while 39% said the same of Republicans.

stories.title: Pakistan conducts maiden flight test of locally developed Fa’az air-to-air missile
summary: Read: Pakistan Army successfully test-fires extended-range Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile It added that the successful flight test demonstrated the "technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance" achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Army successfully test-fired the extended-range version of its Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile, which was equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

Also Read: Pakistan test-fires Fatah-4 missile The ISPR had said the missile was capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating enemy missile defence systems because of its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability.

stories.title: IHC suspends order rejecting FIR plea in Pims fire case, seeks inquiry report and govt response
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order dismissing an application seeking the registration of an FIR into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) neonatal fire tragedy.

The court also directed the authorities to submit the complete record, along with the inquiry report, and issued notices to the respondents, including the federal government and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
After hearing the arguments, the court suspended the Justice of the Peace’s order and directed the authorities to submit the complete record, including the inquiry reports, before the next hearing.

stories.title: Petitions against detention of Sohail Afridi, others referred to PHC CJ for constitution of larger bench
summary: PESHAWAR: A Peshawar High Court (PHC) bench on Tuesday referred multiple petitions challenging the detention of PTI leaders, including Sohail Afridi — the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister — to the chief justice for the constitution of a larger bench.
It further observed that the detentions under consideration were not MPO cases. “This is an important case; the chief minister of the province is missing,” Justice Ali observed.

The bench said the court had given the respondents 10 days to file replies, but they had not complied with the order. “We refer this case to the chief justice to constitute a larger bench,” Justice Ali said.

stories.title: Trump says US will stop $4 billion in funding to Israel at end of 2026
summary: President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made ​a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of ‌this year.

It was not immediately clear which funding Trump meant or how exactly the funding would be stopped at the end of the year, given that the memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8 billion in US military aid to Israel each year does not expire until 2028.

Speaking to Fox News' "Fox & Friends" programme, Trump said Israel no longer needed ​the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as ⁠a talking point to criticise Republicans.

stories.title: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
summary: Read: Nine terrorists killed in two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR The first operation was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district, where security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock, killing 10 of them.
President Asif Ali Zardari praised the security forces for killing the 17 terrorists in the two operations.

Also Read: Terrorist killed in intelligence-based operation in Balochistan's Kech district: state media Zardari said the soldier’s sacrifice for the defence, peace and security of the country would always be remembered.

stories.title: Foreign women rape case: Incomplete police report clears five suspects of sexual assault charges
summary: LAHORE: An incomplete investigation report (challan) filed before a trial court in connection with the alleged gang rape of two foreign women in July cleared five suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, of sexual assault charges.
However, according to the police report, the women did not pay him any profits or return his investment this time.
Therefore, the police submitted an incomplete investigation report to avoid delays, despite having sufficient evidence against the suspects.

stories.title: Chinese researchers achieve breakthrough in underground positioning and navigation
summary: Developed under the name "Xingyuan," the BeiDou micro-base-station system for underground positioning and navigation extends high-precision location services into spaces beyond the reach of satellite signals.

CETC54 engineer Chen Chong said the system offers more than convenience, opening up new possibilities for intelligent transportation, mining and other sectors and reflecting the expanding use of high-precision positioning technology underground.

Satellite navigation has long faced challenges in underground car parks because satellite signals cannot penetrate underground structures, making accurate positioning on ordinary smartphones difficult and leaving gaps in navigation services.

stories.title: Respect for a woman’s dignity not just a matter of personal morality but constitutional obligation: Supreme Court
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) stated on Tuesday that respect for a woman’s dignity was not merely a matter of personal morality but a constitutional obligation the state expected of everyone in its service.

His character, integrity and conduct in private life may also become relevant where these factors bore upon his suitability to hold a public office, the discipline of the service or public confidence in the institution he served, Justice Waheed emphasised.
It is that the petitioner set his wife on fire, an act which, if established, is among the gravest forms of violence one person can inflict upon another,” the judgement said.

stories.title: China's Baidu launches AI model simulating road environment for robotaxis
summary: China's Baidu launched Apollo World on Tuesday, an ‌AI system designed to simulate real-world environments for training robotaxis and predict how they evolve, as automakers race to cut the cost of developing autonomous vehicles.

Apollo World can generate "up to 100,000 ​km" (62,000 miles) of simulated driving daily, equivalent to about three years of ​real-world testing by a safety-driver-equipped autonomous vehicle, Baidu said.
Baidu said Apollo ​World is already being used for training Apollo Go’s robotaxi fleet to be operated globally.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45, HSD by Rs3.68 for Nov 4
summary: The announcement came after the government earlier today said that consumers could expect further "good news" on petroleum prices, adding that it was taking steps to address excessive liquid petroleum gas prices by opening up the market to competition.

He added that the government had taken all possible measures to provide relief to consumers, keeping in view the country's economic constraints, and had extended Rs130 billion in subsidies under its public relief scheme.

Malik further stated the government would also ensure fair distribution of LPG quotas for hard-to-reach areas and was exploring measures to extend relief to vulnerable consumers in the gas sector, including through assistance from the Benazir Income Support Programme.

stories.title: LPG soars in Pakistan, forcing rickshaw drivers to cut meals

Ali, 33, is among thousands of Pakistani drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly ​used for cooking and heating.

"Now, it's just not possible to get by on seven or eight hundred [rupees], is it?" Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of ​LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said.
